Theorem
[First Existence Theorem for weak solutions] ↗ thm:lax-milgram-theorem ↗ thm:energy-estimates ↗ def:bilinear-form-weak-solution-l2 1. ch6:6.2-thm-3\group Weak Solutions

There is a number $\gamma \geq 0$ such that for each \[ (7) \qquad \mu \geq \gamma \] and each function \[ f \in L^2(U), \] there exists a unique weak solution $u \in H_0^1(U)$ of the boundary-value problem \[ (8) \qquad \begin{cases} Lu + \mu u = f & \text{in } U \\ u = 0 & \text{on } \partial U \end{cases} \]

Proof

\sketch For $\mu \ge \gamma $, the shifted form $B_\mu [u,v]=B[u,v]+\mu (u,v)$ is bounded and coercive. Apply Lax–Milgram to the functional $v\mapsto (f,v)$.

□
